meta.title: Trams and trolleybuses
meta.pdd: The Rules: paras. 2(47), 20-21, 30, 33, 41, 52, 65, 87(1), (7), 91, 97, 101, 103-104, 106, 111, 125-127, 155, Annex 1 (signs 5.9, 5.12, 5.13); Basic Provisions on Admitting Vehicles to Operation, para. 9; Road Traffic Act, arts. 73-74; Examination Rules, paras. 7, 11
meta.summary: You will learn what you need for categories Tm and Tb, how to read the traffic light shaped like the letter “T”, when a tram has priority and when it gives way, and what the Rules require of tram and trolleybus drivers at stops.

p: Trams are category Tm, trolleybuses are category Tb ⟦18⟧. A category D licence does not cover trolleybuses: apart from category D buses, it entitles you only to subcategory D1.

Category Tm is granted from the age of 21, and the law requires no driving experience. Category Tb is granted from the age of 23 with at least three years of experience as a driver, including at least one year on subcategory D1 vehicles (art. 74). Some websites still give an age of 25 and 5 years of experience: that is the version of the law in force before 2024.

The practical test for a tram or trolleybus is conducted by a training organisation, not at a specialised PSC test ground ⟦19⟧. The theory test is common to all categories: if you apply for several categories, you take it once ⟦20⟧.

lesson.h: Trams and trolleybuses under the Rules
p: Both trams and trolleybuses are route vehicles, that is, public transport carrying passengers along a fixed route ⟦21⟧.

The main difference for the Rules: a tram is a rail vehicle, while a trolleybus is a trackless vehicle. Every rule that mentions a “trackless vehicle” also applies to trolleybuses. For example, at an intersection of roads of equal status, a trolleybus gives way to a tram.
For trams, and also for public transport in a dedicated lane, traffic lights with four round lunar white signals arranged in the shape of the letter “T” are used ⟦22⟧.

Movement is permitted only when the bottom signal is lit at the same time as one or more of the top signals. The top left signal permits a left turn, the top middle one straight ahead, and the top right one a right turn. The top signals without the bottom one do not permit movement.

lesson.h: The traffic controller and the tram
list: Arms extended to the sides or lowered: from the controller's left and right sides, a tram may only go straight ahead, and trackless vehicles straight ahead and to the right; from the chest and back sides, all vehicles are prohibited from moving ⟦23⟧
Right arm extended forward: from the controller's left side, a tram may turn left, and trackless vehicles may go in all directions ⟦24⟧
Right arm extended forward: from the chest side, all vehicles, including trams, may only turn right; from the right side and the back, movement is prohibited ⟦25⟧
Arm raised: all vehicles are prohibited from moving, except those that can no longer stop without emergency braking ⟦26⟧
A traffic light or traffic controller permits a tram and trackless vehicles to move at the same time: the tram has priority regardless of its direction of travel ⟦27⟧
At an intersection of roads of equal status, a tram has priority over trackless vehicles regardless of the direction of travel ⟦28⟧
Outside intersections, where tram tracks cross the carriageway, a tram has priority over trackless vehicles ⟦29⟧
A tram moving in the direction of a filter arrow lit together with a red or amber signal gives way to vehicles from other directions ⟦30⟧
A tram on a minor road gives way to vehicles on the main road, regardless of their direction ⟦31⟧
A tram leaving the depot has no priority outside an intersection ⟦32⟧

Trams among themselves: at an intersection of roads of equal status, a tram gives way to the one on its right; when turning left or making a U-turn, including on a green signal, it gives way to an oncoming tram going straight ahead or turning right ⟦33⟧
As a tram driver, you also give way to pedestrians on an uncontrolled crossing and to pedestrians on the carriageway you are turning into ⟦34⟧
All drivers give way to vehicles with blue and (or) red flashing beacons and a siren switched on ⟦35⟧
lesson.tip: A tram has priority only over trackless vehicles, and not everywhere.

p: It is useful for a tram driver to know what others are required to do. Tram tracks for the same direction, on the left and level with the carriageway, may be used when all lanes are occupied, and also when going around an obstruction, overtaking, turning left or making a U-turn, but without impeding the tram. Entering tracks for the oncoming direction is prohibited ⟦36⟧.

When turning left or making a U-turn from the tram tracks, a driver gives way to the tram ⟦37⟧. Stopping in the immediate vicinity of the tracks is prohibited if it impedes trams ⟦38⟧. But do not count on everyone following these rules: be ready to stop.

list: Boarding and alighting take place only after a complete stop; you move off only with the doors closed and do not open them until the vehicle has come to a complete stop ⟦39⟧
The driver of a route vehicle lets passengers board and alight only at a designated stop ⟦40⟧
If passengers board from the carriageway, drivers of other vehicles give way to pedestrians walking to or from the tram on the door side ⟦41⟧
Passengers wait on the boarding platform or, if there is none, on the pavement or shoulder; they step onto the carriageway towards the tram only after it has stopped ⟦42⟧
Sign 5.12 is the “Bus and (or) trolleybus stop” sign, sign 5.13 is the “Tram stop” sign (Annex 1)
Other vehicles must not stop in the stop area or within 15 m of it, or, if there is no stop area, within 15 m of the sign marking the stop; the exception is vehicles of categories M2 and M3 ⟦43⟧

lesson.h: Trolleybus: moving off from a stop and the dedicated lane
p: In built-up areas, drivers give way to trolleybuses and buses that are running on their route and moving off from a designated stop. But the trolleybus driver moves off only after making sure that others are giving way ⟦44⟧, and switches on the direction indicator in advance ⟦45⟧.
The lane for route vehicles (sign 5.9) is used by route vehicles, other public transport and vehicles of category M3 ⟦46⟧. It may have the same T-shaped traffic light as trams ⟦47⟧.

Articulated buses and trolleybuses are fitted with the “Road train” identification sign: three amber lamps in a horizontal row on the cab roof, spaced 150 to 300 mm apart (Basic Provisions on Admitting Vehicles to Operation, para. 9).

keyFacts: Tm: from the age of 21, no driving experience required ⟦1⟧
Tb: from the age of 23 with at least 3 years of experience as a driver, including at least one year on D1 (art. 74)
The practical test for Tm and Tb is conducted by a training organisation ⟦2⟧
T-shaped traffic light: only the bottom signal together with a top one permits movement ⟦3⟧
A signal permitting both a tram and trackless vehicles to go: the tram has priority ⟦4⟧
On a filter arrow shown with a red or amber signal, the tram gives way ⟦5⟧
At an intersection of roads of equal status, a tram has priority over trackless vehicles; among trams, the “give way to the right” rule applies ⟦6⟧
On a minor road, a tram gives way ⟦7⟧
Outside an intersection, a tram has priority, except when leaving the depot ⟦8⟧
Doors are opened only after a complete stop; a route vehicle picks up passengers only at a designated stop ⟦9⟧
In a built-up area, others give way to a trolleybus moving off from a designated stop, but it moves off only after making sure they are giving way ⟦10⟧
Articulated trolleybus: the “Road train” sign (Basic Provisions, para. 9)
mistakes: “A tram always has priority”. On a minor road it gives way ⟦11⟧, on a filter arrow shown with a red or amber signal it also gives way ⟦12⟧, and when leaving the depot it has no priority ⟦13⟧.
“You can drive a trolleybus with category D”. You need the separate category Tb ⟦14⟧.
“All three top white signals are lit, so you can go”. Without the bottom signal, movement is not permitted ⟦15⟧.
“In a traffic jam near a stop, you can let passengers off”. A route vehicle lets passengers board and alight only at a designated stop ⟦16⟧.
“A trolleybus moving off from a stop is always in the right”. The driver moves off only after making sure that others are giving way ⟦17⟧.
“You must be 25 for Tm”. That is the old version of the law; Tm is now granted from the age of 21 (art. 74).

questions.q: You are driving a tram. These signals have come on at the tram traffic light. What do they permit?
options: Straight ahead and right
Movement is prohibited
Left and straight ahead
Straight ahead only
questions.explain: The bottom signal and two top signals, the left and the middle one, are lit. On a T-shaped traffic light, the top left signal together with the bottom one permits a left turn and the middle one permits going straight ahead; the right one is not lit, so you may not turn right.

questions.q: You are driving a tram. Which directions does this traffic light signal permit?
options: Left and right
Straight ahead only
All directions
Movement is prohibited
questions.explain: The bottom signal and the top left and top right signals are lit. The top left one permits a left turn, the top right one a right turn. The middle one is not lit, so you may not go straight ahead.

questions.q: What registration numbers must a tram have?
options: State number plates at the front and rear
None: a tram runs only on rails
The route number on the windscreen
Numbers assigned by the relevant authority
questions.explain: State registration plates are fitted to motor vehicles, except trams and trolleybuses. Trams and trolleybuses are marked with registration numbers assigned by the relevant authorities (Basic Provisions on Admitting Vehicles, para. 3).

questions.q: You are driving a tram and intend to turn right. Which traffic light signal permits this?
options: A
B
C
D
questions.explain: A right turn is permitted by the top right signal lit together with the bottom one: that is D. Signal A permits straight ahead only, B permits a left turn only, and C, without the bottom signal, does not permit movement.

questions.q: You are driving a trolleybus in a dedicated lane for route vehicles. This traffic light is installed for the lane. May you go straight ahead?
options: Yes, since the bottom signal is lit
No: only a right turn is permitted now
Yes: a trolleybus need not obey this type of traffic light
No: movement is prohibited in all directions
questions.explain: Traffic lights with lunar white signals arranged in the shape of the letter “T” are also used for public transport in a dedicated lane. The bottom and top right signals are lit: only a right turn is permitted.

questions.q: Who are traffic lights with four lunar white signals arranged in the shape of the letter “T” used for?
options: Pedestrians and cyclists at controlled crossings
All vehicles at level crossings
Trams and public transport in a dedicated lane
All vehicles in lanes with reversible traffic
questions.explain: Such traffic lights control the movement of trams and public transport in a dedicated lane ⟦48⟧. The flashing lunar white signal at a level crossing belongs to a different traffic light ⟦49⟧, and reversible lanes use traffic lights with a red X-shaped signal and a green arrow pointing down ⟦50⟧.

questions.q: You are driving a tram. The traffic controller is standing with their chest towards you, with the right arm extended forward. Where may you go?
options: Straight ahead only
Left only
Right only
Movement is prohibited
questions.explain: When the traffic controller's right arm is extended forward, all vehicles approaching from the chest side, including trams, may only turn right. From the right side and the back, movement is prohibited, and from the left side a tram may turn left.

questions.q: You are driving a tram. The traffic controller is standing with their right side towards you, with the right arm extended forward. Where are you allowed to go?
options: Movement is prohibited
Left only
Straight ahead only
Straight ahead and right
questions.explain: The right arm is extended forward: from the traffic controller's right side and back, all vehicles are prohibited from moving. If you were approaching from the controller's left side, a tram would be allowed to turn left.

questions.q: An intersection of roads of equal status. You are driving a tram straight ahead, and a green car is approaching from the right. Who goes first?
options: The green car: it is on the right
The tram
Whoever arrived first
The tram, but only if it sounds its horn
questions.explain: At an intersection of roads of equal status, a tram has priority over trackless vehicles regardless of its direction of travel. The “give way to the right” rule applies between trackless vehicles and between trams.

questions.q: You are driving a tram straight ahead. There is a 2.4 “Give way” sign for your direction before the intersection. A green car is approaching from the right on the main road. Who goes first?
options: The tram: it always has priority
Whoever arrived first
The tram, if the car is turning
The green car
questions.explain: A tram's priority applies at an intersection of roads of equal status and when one signal permits both it and trackless vehicles to go. At an intersection of roads of unequal status, whoever is on the minor road gives way to vehicles on the main road, and a tram is no exception.

questions.q: You are driving a tram straight ahead on the main road. In what order will the vehicles pass through the intersection?
options: Tram, white, blue
White, tram, blue
Tram, blue, white
Blue, tram, white
questions.explain: The blue car on the minor road gives way to everyone on the main road. The white car on the main road is turning left and gives way to the oncoming tram going straight ahead. So the tram goes first, then the white car, and the blue car last.

questions.q: The light is green for you and for oncoming traffic. You are driving a tram straight ahead, and an oncoming white car is turning left. Who goes first?
options: The white car
Both at the same time
The tram
Whoever entered the intersection first
questions.explain: If a traffic light signal permits a tram and trackless vehicles to move at the same time, the tram has priority. Besides, a car turning left gives way to oncoming traffic.

questions.q: You are driving a tram and turning right on the green filter arrow, while the main signal is red. Who has priority?
options: You: a tram always has priority
No one: all vehicles go at the same time
Vehicles from other directions: you give way
Pedestrians, but not cars
questions.explain: When moving in the direction of a filter arrow lit together with a red or amber signal, a tram gives way to vehicles coming from other directions. The tram's priority does not apply here.

questions.q: You are driving a tram out of the depot. The tracks cross the carriageway outside an intersection, and cars are moving along it. Who has priority?
options: The cars: a tram leaving the depot gives way
The tram: outside intersections it has priority in any case
Whoever sounded the horn first
The tram, but only with its headlights on
questions.explain: Outside intersections, where tram tracks cross the carriageway, a tram has priority over trackless vehicles. The exception is leaving the depot: then the tram driver lets the traffic on the road go first.

questions.q: You are driving a tram on its route. Ahead, the tracks cross the carriageway outside an intersection, and a car is approaching the crossing point at the same time as you. Who goes first?
options: The car: it is on the carriageway
Whoever is on the right
Whoever sounds the horn
The tram
questions.explain: Outside intersections, where tram tracks cross the carriageway, a tram has priority over trackless vehicles. You are not leaving the depot, so you have priority.

questions.q: You are driving a tram. Ahead there is an uncontrolled pedestrian crossing, and a pedestrian is walking across it. What should you do?
options: Sound the horn and drive on: the tram has priority
Give way to the pedestrian
Drive on if the pedestrian has not yet reached the tracks
Drive on: the pedestrian must let the tram pass
questions.explain: At an uncontrolled pedestrian crossing, a driver gives way to pedestrians crossing the carriageway in the driver's direction of travel. This also applies to a tram driver: a tram has priority only over trackless vehicles.

questions.q: The light is green for you. An ambulance with its flashing beacons and siren on is approaching the intersection from the left. Who goes first?
options: The tram: it has a green light and priority
Both at the same time
The ambulance
Whoever is closer to the intersection
questions.explain: When a vehicle with blue and (or) red flashing beacons and a siren switched on is approaching, drivers give way to it, including the tram driver. The tram's priority does not cancel this.

questions.q: An oncoming blue car is standing on the tram tracks and turning left. You are driving a tram straight ahead. Who goes first?
options: The blue car: it is already on the tracks
Both at the same time
Whoever signalled the turn first
The tram
questions.explain: When turning left from the tram tracks, the driver of a trackless vehicle gives way to the tram. But do not count on the driver letting you through: slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.q: All lanes in the same direction are occupied, and a car is driving along the tram tracks ahead of your tram. The track is on the left, level with the carriageway. Is the car driver breaking the Rules?
options: No, if the driver does not impede the tram
Yes: driving on tram tracks is always prohibited
No, and the tram must follow it indefinitely
Yes: tram tracks may be used only for turning
questions.explain: Driving on tram tracks for the same direction, located on the left and level with the carriageway, is permitted when all lanes in that direction are occupied. The driver must not impede the tram while doing so.

questions.q: A car going around a traffic jam is driving along the tram tracks towards your tram. Is its driver breaking the Rules?
options: No, if the driver quickly returns to their own lane
Yes: entering the oncoming tram tracks is prohibited
No, if the oncoming tram is still far away
No: going around a jam on the tracks is allowed
questions.explain: Trackless vehicles may use only tram tracks for the same direction located on the left. Entering tracks for the oncoming direction is prohibited, since trams come the other way on them.

questions.q: A car has stopped so close to the tram tracks that your tram cannot get past. Has its driver broken the Rules?
options: No, if the stop is short, no longer than five minutes
No, if the hazard warning lights are on
Yes, but only if the driver has left the car
Yes: you must not stop near the tracks and impede trams
questions.explain: The Rules prohibit stopping in the immediate vicinity of tram tracks if this impedes the movement of trams. How long the stop lasts and whether the hazard warning lights are on make no difference.

questions.q: A broken-down trolleybus with passengers on board has to be towed to the depot on a rigid tow bar. May the passengers stay inside?
options: Yes, if the speed does not exceed 50 km/h
No: a towed trolleybus must not carry passengers
Yes, if all the passengers are seated
Yes: the ban applies only to towing on a tow rope
questions.explain: When towing with a tow rope or a rigid tow bar, passengers must not be carried in the towed bus or trolleybus ⟦51⟧. Passengers are let off before towing begins.

questions.q: Your tram is still rolling towards the stop, but you have already opened the doors to save time. Have you broken the Rules?
options: No, if the speed is very low
No, if the passengers are holding the handrails
Yes: doors are opened after a complete stop
No, if only the front door is open
questions.explain: The driver moves off only with the doors closed and does not open them until the vehicle has come to a complete stop. Getting off while the vehicle is moving is dangerous: a passenger may fall under the wheels.

questions.q: Your trolleybus is stuck in a traffic jam 50 m from the stop. Passengers ask you to let them off right here. May you open the doors?
options: No: passengers alight only at a designated stop
Yes: the trolleybus is standing still anyway
Yes, if you open only the front door
Yes, if the stop is less than 100 m away
questions.explain: The driver of a route vehicle lets passengers board and alight only at a designated stop. In the middle of a traffic jam, people would step out between cars onto the carriageway.

questions.q: Everyone has boarded, but a late passenger is still holding one of the tram doors open. May you move off so as not to fall behind schedule?
options: Yes, if you move off very slowly
Yes, if only the rear door is open
Yes, if you give a warning with the horn first
No: you move off only with the doors closed
questions.explain: A driver may move off only with the doors closed. Keeping to the schedule does not justify the risk of a passenger being caught in the door or falling.

questions.q: You are driving a trolleybus on its route and moving off from a designated stop in town. A green car is approaching from behind in the next lane. What should you do?
options: Pull away at once without indicating: everyone must give way to you
Indicate and move off after making sure others give way
Wait until there is not a single car left on the whole street
Sound the horn and pull out into the next lane at once
questions.explain: In built-up areas, drivers give way to trolleybuses and buses moving off from a designated stop. But the trolleybus driver moves off only after making sure that others are giving way, and switches on the direction indicator before the manoeuvre.

questions.q: A police officer has stopped your trolleybus away from a stop. The check is over, and you are moving off from the edge of the road. Must drivers in the next lane let you out?
options: Yes: others always give way to a trolleybus
Yes, if you switch on the hazard warning lights
No: that rule applies only at a stop
Yes, if there are passengers on board now
questions.explain: Drivers give way to a trolleybus or bus that is running on its route and moving off from a designated stop ⟦52⟧. Away from a stop there is no such rule: you move off without impeding other road users and let those in the next lane go first ⟦53⟧.

questions.q: You are driving a trolleybus. Which sign marks a stopping place on your route?
options: A
B
Both
Neither
questions.explain: Sign 5.12 “Bus and (or) trolleybus stop” marks a stopping place for buses and (or) trolleybuses. Sign 5.13 “Tram stop” marks a stopping place for trams.

questions.q: In your trolleybus, you are approaching a stop that has no stop area. A car is standing 10 m before the sign marking the stop and prevents you from pulling in to the edge of the carriageway. Has its driver broken the Rules?
options: No, if the driver is only letting a passenger out
No: this prohibition applies only to trucks
No, if it stays there no longer than 5 minutes
Yes: stopping within 15 m of that sign is prohibited
questions.explain: If there is no stop area, stopping is prohibited within 15 m of the sign marking a route vehicle stop or taxi rank. The only exception is for vehicles of categories M2 and M3, and a passenger car is not one of them.

questions.q: You are driving a trolleybus on its route. On the right there is a lane for route vehicles. May you move into it and carry on?
options: Yes: the lane is for route vehicles, like trolleybuses
No: this lane is intended for use by buses only
Yes, but only at rush hour and on weekdays
Yes, but only if there are no passengers on board
questions.explain: The lane marked with sign 5.9 is used by route vehicles, other public transport and vehicles of category M3. A trolleybus is a route vehicle, so this lane is for you, and the broken line allows you to move into it.

questions.q: At a controlled intersection, the green signal permits both your tram and oncoming cars to proceed. You are turning left, and an oncoming car is going straight ahead. Who goes first?
options: The oncoming car
The tram
Both at the same time
Whoever entered the intersection first
questions.explain: If the signals of a traffic light or traffic controller permit a tram and trackless vehicles to move at the same time, the tram has priority regardless of its direction of travel. So even when turning left, the tram goes first.

questions.q: Two tram lines cross at an intersection of roads of equal status. You are driving a tram straight ahead, and another tram is approaching from the right. Who goes first?
options: You: a tram always has priority
Whoever sounded the horn
Both at the same time
The tram on the right
questions.explain: Among themselves, tram drivers at an intersection of roads of equal status follow the same rule as trackless vehicles: they give way to the one approaching from the right.

questions.q: An intersection of roads of equal status. You are turning left in your tram, and another tram is coming from the opposite direction, going straight ahead. Who goes first?
options: You, since you are already turning
Both at the same time
The oncoming tram
Whoever sounds the horn
questions.explain: When turning left, you give way to those coming from the opposite direction on a road of equal status and going straight ahead or turning right. Tram drivers follow the same rule among themselves.

questions.q: You are turning right in your tram on a green signal. Pedestrians are crossing the carriageway you are turning into. What should you do?
options: Drive on: the tram has priority
Sound the horn and drive on
Give way to the pedestrians
Drive on if the pedestrians have not yet reached the tracks
questions.explain: When turning right or left, a driver gives way to pedestrians crossing the carriageway of the road onto which the driver is turning. A tram's priority concerns trackless vehicles, not pedestrians.

questions.q: What is the minimum age for obtaining the right to drive a tram (category Tm)?
options: 18 years
21 years
23 years
25 years
questions.explain: The right to drive category Tm vehicles is granted from the age of 21, and the law requires no driving experience for it. Websites that say 25 are repeating the version of the law in force before 2024.

questions.q: What requirements does the law set for someone who wants to obtain category Tb (trolleybuses)?
options: From age 23, with at least 3 years as a driver, at least 1 of them on D1
From age 18, with no experience needed, as for category B
From age 21, with at least 1 year of experience as a driver
From age 25, with at least 5 years as a driver, at least 3 of them on D1
questions.explain: Under the current version of article 74, categories D and Tb are granted from the age of 23 with at least three years of experience as a driver, including at least one year driving subcategory D1 vehicles.

questions.q: Who conducts the practical test for driving a tram or trolleybus?
options: The automated test ground of a specialised PSC
Any driver holding category D
A police officer on a city route
A training organisation
questions.explain: Under the Examination Rules, the practical test for driving a tram or trolleybus is conducted by a training organisation. For the other categories, the practical test is taken at a test ground of the State Corporation (specialised PSC).

questions.q: A driver holds a category D licence. May they drive a trolleybus?
options: Yes: a trolleybus is driven the same way as a bus
No: a trolleybus requires category Tb
Yes, if the trolleybus has no passengers
Yes, but only within their own town
questions.explain: The law puts trolleybuses in a separate category, Tb, and trams in Tm. Apart from category D itself, such a licence covers only subcategory D1.

questions.q: You are setting off on a route in an articulated trolleybus. Which identification sign must it carry?
options: “Oversized load” at the front and rear
“Speed limit” on the back of the body
“Road train”: three amber lamps on the roof
None: trolleybuses do not carry such signs
questions.explain: The “Road train” sign is three amber lamps in a horizontal row on the cab roof, spaced 150 to 300 mm apart. It is fitted to trucks and wheeled tractors with trailers, and also to articulated buses and trolleybuses.

questions.q: In your tram, you are approaching a stop without a boarding platform. People waiting for the tram are standing on the carriageway next to the tracks. Are they acting correctly?
options: Yes: that way they board the tram faster
No: they must wait on the pavement or shoulder
Yes, if the tram is still far away
Yes, if they stand on a road marking line
questions.explain: People wait for a route vehicle on the boarding platform or, if there is none, on the pavement or shoulder. They may step onto the carriageway to board only after the vehicle has stopped. If you see people on the carriageway, slow down and be ready to stop.
